images.caption: Figure 1:(a) An example from PMC-VQA[55], where Qwen3.5-4B writes 1,024 tokens without selecting an option andMedJev-4B scores the candidates in one forward pass. (b) Per-request latency against generated tokens, thinking off. (c) Average accuracy and latency on four benchmarks, whereMedJev-4B beats all 20 general and medical VLMs at the 4B–9B scale on both.

Figure 2:Overview ofMedJev.(a) The images, the question, and all candidates form a single prompt with learned markers, and every visual token is kept. (b) A reduced backbone returns the marker states. (c) Pretrained query–key matching and a shared MLP residual score the candidates in one pass. The example is a CT question of PMC-VQA[55]with the probabilities ofMedJev-4B.
Figure 6:One PMC-VQA case under both interfaces.The backbone decodes a sentence that names the wrong bones, whileMedJev-4B scores all four candidates in one pass and picks the reference.

Figure A1:Calibration and per-category behaviour of the deployed model.(a) Accuracy against confidence in fifteen equal-width bins over all 36,286 test examples.
(b) Accuracy on the answered cases when the least confident ones are referred away.
(c) The confusion on HAM10000, each row normalized by the test cases of that category.
(d) The recall of each category with its counts.

Figure A2:Hidden representations in detail.Each panel is reduced on its own, so its layout
is never driven by the others. (a) and (b) give one column per benchmark, the decision marker state at
layer 23 before and after training, and the candidate marker states of the trained model split by
whether the candidate is correct. (c) gives the same split at four depths of the pretrained backbone.
